text: Deadlines are a part of professional life, and handling them well requires a few key skills. First, effective time management is crucial. Breaking a large project into smaller, daily tasks makes it feel less overwhelming and helps you track your progress. Next, learn to prioritize. Not every task carries the same weight, so focus on the most important or urgent items first. It is also wise to practice scope management. If a project keeps growing with new requests, you need to politely clarify the original goals to avoid overcommitting. Finally, keep communication open. If you foresee a problem meeting a deadline, inform your team or client early. People are usually more understanding when they have time to adjust their plans.
